reason: Codex harness /goal failed on every call: _codex_feature_policy lists goals among the managed vendor features but never enabled it, so Core launched codex app-server with features.goals=false and codex-cli 0.154.0 answers thread/goal/set and thread/goal/get with 'goals feature is disabled' (reproduced against the real binary; the fake RPC in test_harness_commands never checked the flag). Enabling it exposes Codex's goal runtime, which starts the next turn of an active goal on its own about 1-2 s after each turn completes, so CodexAppServerConnection.run_turn now follows turn/started notifications for its own thread while the last goal update said active, until the goal completes, pauses or hits a limit, or no continuation arrives within 15 s. A Stop between two goal turns cancels the reader task first, so interrupt() pauses the goal (Codex then starts no further turn) and interrupts any turn _CodexRpc recorded as already running. Verified end to end against real Codex: /goal ran four vendor turns inside one Nebula turn to status complete, and a Stop in the gap left the goal paused with no new turn for 10 s. test_harness_adapters.py carries the new tests (feature flag in process overrides and thread config, following continuation turns while ignoring another thread's turn/started, timeout, paused-while-waiting, stop in the gap with and without a started turn, running-turn tracking in _CodexRpc); the other files are the suites that drive CodexAppServerConnection, _run_harness_command or the harness runtime.
exclusions: Backend-only change inside the Codex connection and its RPC reader; no UI, API shape or native code changed, so no frontend, Playwright or native tests apply. Grok and Claude connections are untouched. test_browser_companion.py is left out: it only calls CodexAppServerAdapter._models, which this change does not touch, and it needs a real Chromium (it passes locally with one).
